hook: MISREP 4472514 is a U.S. Air Force mission report documenting three separate UAP observations made by a single long-endurance ISR aircraft (482 ATKS, 432 AEW) over the Arabian Gulf, Strait of Hormuz, and Gulf of Oman on July 16–17, 2020, across a ~21-hour mission supporting NAVCENT.
why_it_matters: This report is notable for logging three distinct UAP encounters within a single ISR mission, each at different grid locations and times, all recorded via Full Motion Video (FMV). The observations occur during an active intelligence-gathering mission already tracking Iranian naval vessels, establishing that the UAP sightings were incidental to a structured surveillance operation rather than a dedicated UAP hunt. The document was processed through the formal MISREP reporting chain and approved for release to AARO, illustrating the modern institutional pathway for military UAP reporting.

key_findings.finding: Three separate UAP were observed during a single mission at 1830Z, 1920Z, and 2345Z on July 16, 2020, all via Full Motion Video (FMV) sensor.

key_findings.finding: The mission was a ~21-hour long-endurance ISR sortie (AREC type) operated by 482 ATKS out of OKAS, supporting NAVCENT with 24-hour pre-coordination, and was simultaneously tracking probable Iranian naval vessels including NASER, SAFIR KISH, and HOUDONG-class craft.
